judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two lettered conditions and the 'otherwise' fallback allocate cash discounts clearly, though 'trade discounts, rebates, refunds and amounts received from sales of surplus materials' is a list whose edges could be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 9.1.1 [New] adds a seven-day notice and funding opportunity before the Contractor may take any discount for itself, which supplements rather than contradicts this paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line crediting mechanism; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.1, 7.4.2 and the Cost of the Work definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Portions of the Work that the Contractor does not customarily perform with the Contractor's own personnel' turns on an undefined custom, and 'reasonable objection' is a soft standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 6.5 imposes a different procurement regime (at least two bids, Owner- or Architect-named subcontractors, Change Orders awarding the work), and A201 5.2.1-5.2.3 adds another; the three must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three numbered conditions and the difference-in-bids measure are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The remedy is an adjustment of the Guaranteed Maximum Price, which 5.2.1 leaves as 'N/A,' so the mechanism has nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States a monthly period with an unfilled 'or as follows' alternative; the default sentence is complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 12.1.3 and A201 9.3.1; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The payment deadlines depend on fill-in numerals ('not later than the ___ day of a month ... not later than the ___ day of the following month ... ___ days'), which are illegible or incomplete, so the due date cannot be fixed from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.4.1 (seven days to certify), 9.6.1, 9.7.1 (stop-work after seven days from the date 'established in the Contract Documents') and 14.2 interest all key off this date, and First Addendum 12.2.2 supplies different final-payment timing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The equal-or-exceed test with its three numbered components is arithmetically specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 12.1.4 [New] adds a further list of required accompaniments 'in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect,' and 12.1.7.5 lets the Owner deduct the resulting shortfall; the two versions of 12.1.4 coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The drafting is clear on its own terms: allocate the whole price among portions of the Work with the Fee as a single line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires allocation of 'the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price,' which 5.2.1 states as 'N/A,' while First Addendum 6.5 substitutes a Preliminary Budget with an Itemized Schedule of Values estimating the Contract Sum; A201 9.2.1 adds a third formulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lesser-of test is mechanically stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (2) divides by 'the share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocated to that portion,' a share that cannot exist given 5.2.1's 'N/A' and the fast-track budget procedure of Addendum 6.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory stem to the computation clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clauses it introduces are built on the Guaranteed Maximum Price and are revised in part by Addendum 12.1.7.3, but the stem itself adds nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The multiplication formula is precise; only the 'amounts not in dispute' proviso is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It takes 'that portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price properly allocable to completed Work' when no Guaranteed Maximum Price was inserted in 5.2.1; the payment formula therefore cannot be applied literally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard stored-materials add, conditioned on Owner approval for off-site storage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same defect as .1: it measures the payment by the non-existent Guaranteed Maximum Price, though 7.5.6 and A201 9.3.2 supply consistent storage conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Retainage is filled in as 'N/A percent (N/A %)', leaving the deduction from the Fee undefined within a clause that assumes a percentage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 12.1.7.3 [Revision] fixes retainage at five percent, so the executed instrument contains two inconsistent versions of the same clause; 12.1.8 separately imposes 10% on subcontractor payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line arithmetic deduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.2.1 and 13.2.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The shortfall, if any, indicated by the Contractor in the documentation required by Paragraph 12.1.4' is defined only by reference and could be read narrowly or broadly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 12.1.4 as supplemented by First Addendum 12.1.4 [New] and on the Owner's accountants under 12.1.9 and 12.2.3; workable but interdependent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-referenced deduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches A201 9.5.1's withholding grounds; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is misnumbered '12.1.9' although a different 12.1.9 follows, and 'not less than ten percent' sets a floor without a ceiling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Contractor's own retainage is five percent of the Fee under Addendum 12.1.7.3 while subcontractors are retained at ten percent, and A201 9.6.2 requires payment to subcontractors 'reflecting percentages actually retained' from the Contractor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long disclaimer of the Architect's verification duties, drafted with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 9.4.2 and with 12.2.3's role for the Owner's accountants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory sentence stating final payment is the entire unpaid balance of the Contract Sum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 12.2.1 adds a third condition (recorded Notice of Completion) and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 adds another (warranties received and accepted), so the conditions list is not closed where it appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fully performed ... and to satisfy other requirements, if any, which extend beyond final payment' is a residual phrase but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with A201 9.10.2 and 12.2.2; the added Addendum condition does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single objective condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 12.2.1 supplies a further subsection .3 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 bars the final Certificate until warranties are accepted; the enumeration here is therefore incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States 30 days from the Architect's final Certificate with an unfilled 'or as follows' alternative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision] replaces this with fifty days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or five business days after a lien-free title endorsement, whichever is earlier—a direct contradiction of the printed 30-day term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Time periods and the supersession of A201 9.4.1 are stated expressly; 'substantiated by the Contractor's final accounting' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 12.2.2 as revised by the Addendum, with 12.2.4's arbitration right, and with A201 9.10.1; the layered deadlines create timing questions but each is expressly ordered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 30-day forfeiture rule stated plainly, though 'shall result in the substantiated amount ... becoming binding' is a strong consequence resting on one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits a demand for arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect,' while A201 4.5.1 makes mediation a condition precedent to arbitration and 4.6.2-4.6.3 set their own time limits; the interaction is not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reimbursement basis is clear, but the clause caps recovery by the Guaranteed Maximum Price and refers to savings participation 'as provided in Paragraph 5.2,' which the parties left blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.1 supplies no Guaranteed Maximum Price and no savings-sharing provision was inserted, so both limbs of the limitation are unanchored; A201 12.2.2 governs the correction obligation itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap on convenience-termination recovery and the 'as if fully completed' fee calculation are stated, but their interplay is dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.4.3 gives the Contractor termination costs plus profit on the whole Work, and this paragraph limits recovery to the 13.2 for-cause measure with a modified fee; the override is expressed but the two texts pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The ceiling and the three-step calculation are stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The first ceiling is that payment 'shall not cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded,' which is meaningless given 5.2.1's 'N/A'; A201 14.2.4 supplies a different balance-of-Contract-Sum calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single arithmetic step.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 7's definition of Cost of the Work.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: For a fixed-sum fee the ratio depends on 'a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion,' a figure the contract never fixes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same undefined estimate appears in 12.1.7.3, and with no Guaranteed Maximum Price or completed budget in the instrument there is no agreed benchmark; Addendum 6.5's Preliminary Budget is the nearest candidate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single arithmetic step.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 12.1.7.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair compensation, either by purchase or rental at the election of the Owner' fixes no measure of value, and the assignment obligation is broad ('all such papers ... as the Owner may require').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with A201 5.4.1 contingent assignment and 14.2.2; no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference with an express gloss on the word 'profit.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It provides that 'the Guaranteed Maximum Price and Contract Time shall be increased' on suspension, but no Guaranteed Maximum Price exists under 5.2.1; A201 14.3.2 supplies the adjustment machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An interpretive rule about cross-references; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mechanism by which the Supplementary Conditions' revisions attach, and it sits against Article 1's statement that the Agreement governs inconsistencies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate is left as a blank or 'N/A,' so whether the parties agreed no interest or triggered the 'in the absence thereof, legal rate' fallback is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 13.6.1 contains the same default, and 12.1.3's payment date—also a blank—determines when interest starts, so the interest term depends on two unfilled fields.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two names are entered where the form calls for 'the Owner's representative,' leaving it unclear whether either alone may bind the Owner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1 designates Mary Williamson as the authorized representative while allowing action by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson, and Addendum 14.3 [Revised] gives a third formulation; A201 2.1.1 contemplates one representative with express authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entry names one person 'succeeded by' another, which is an unusual way to identify a single current representative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14.5 requires ten days' written notice before either representative is changed, yet a succession is built into the entry itself; Addendum Article 2 [Revised] separately requires designation of a supervisory employee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single notice requirement, plainly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its operation is complicated by the multiple named Owner representatives in 14.3, Addendum 14.3 and Supplementary Condition 2.1.1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is followed by nothing, so the paragraph is empty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7.2.2 and 8.1.1 both carve out costs 'as may be provided in Article 14,' and the First Addendum inserts a new 14.6 of warranties—so the blank both defeats two cross-references and is overwritten elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory sentence to the enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The enumeration it introduces is itself revised by the Addendum, but the stem creates no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple identification of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 15.1.1 [Revision] restates it as the Agreement 'as modified by the First Addendum,' which is the fix for Article 1's precedence language rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence identifies 'the 1991 edition' of the General Conditions and then cites A201-1997, an internal date mismatch in a single line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 15.1.2 [Revision] and the Supplementary Conditions both identify the 1997 Edition as modified, so the edition question is answered elsewhere but not here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It incorporates Specifications 'contained in the Project Manual dated as in Subparagraph 15.1.3' and then lists none, so the incorporated text is unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.3 records the Project Manual as 'n/a'/TBD, yet A201 1.1.1, 1.1.6 and 1.2.1 treat the Specifications as a core Contract Document and 1.2.1.1 resolves inconsistencies among them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Drawings are 'as follows' with nothing following and a 'TBD' date, so the graphic portion of the Contract Documents is unidentified on the face of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.6 and Addendum 6.5 assume Drawings that will be developed, Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(a) gives given dimensions precedence over scaled measurements, and A201 1.1.5 and 3.2.1 presuppose a defined set.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entries are identified by title and page count; the trailing sentence about bidding requirements is boilerplate for a document 'not intended for use in competitive bidding.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It classifies the First Addendum and Supplementary Conditions—documents that amend the Agreement and A201—as 'Addenda,' which under Article 1 are 'other Contract Documents' subordinate to the Agreement they modify.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of exhibits identified by letter and title; nothing ambiguous in the listing itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits C and D contain substantive pricing rules (5% hand-tool add-on, 1% insurance rate, excise-tax treatment) that sit against Articles 7 and 8, while Article 1 says the Agreement governs inconsistencies with other Contract Documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The article consists of the form's bracketed instruction to insert required limits of liability, with no limits inserted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 11.1.2 requires coverage 'for not less than limits ... specified in the Contract Documents or required by law,' and A201 11.4.1 assumes an insurable 'initial Contract Sum'; with Article 16 blank and no Contract Sum stated, the insurance obligations lack a benchmark.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Execution and distribution of counterparts; routine.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.5.1 on signing the Contract Documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital of attachment and purpose ('modifying, supplementing, and amending certain terms'); it identifies parties and a date but creates no operative right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It recites an Agreement 'dated February 1, 2002' while the Agreement itself is made as of a differently expressed date, and its amending purpose runs against Article 1's rule that the Agreement governs inconsistencies with other Contract Documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only skilled and properly trained staff,' 'appropriately skilled and experienced supervisory employee' who shall 'personally supervise and attend to the Work,' and other work permitted only where it does not 'impair his or her ability' are all evaluative standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the original Article 2 and overlaps A201 3.9.1's competent-superintendent requirement, so the personnel obligation is stated in three places with different wording.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits' does not say whether commencement is postponed until permits issue or merely anticipated, which is the sort of phrase parties read two ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.2 measures the Contract Time from commencement while revised 4.3 fixes a calendar completion date of November 30, 2003, so a permit-driven delay in commencement has no stated effect on the completion obligation or the 4.4 bonus.
